maps.title: Great powers & empires, 1914
maps.blurb: Interactive state-level overview on 1914 borders: each polity painted by its overall religious majority. District-level maps (Russian uyezds, Ottoman vilayets, German kreise) are listed below and still need historic census GIS.
maps.source: Borders: historical-basemaps world_1914. Plurality coding by birthrate.io.
maps.statusNote: World overview paused — rendering on full-world historic basemaps was unreliable. Empire-specific maps (starting with Austria-Hungary) are being built instead.

maps.title: Religions in the Russian Empire, 1897
maps.blurb: Interactive 1897 religion map: Orthodox core, Protestant Baltics, Catholic Congress Poland, Muslim Volga–Caucasus–Central Asia, Buddhist Kalmyk/Buryat steppe — modern provinces inside the 1914 outline (Finland omitted; no Prussian/Habsburg Poland).
maps.source: Russian Empire Census 1897 (religion). Cartographic inspiration: forummapping.

maps.title: Ethnoreligious communities in the Ottoman Empire, c. 1914
maps.blurb: Vilayet- and sanjak-level Muslim, Greek Orthodox, Armenian, Jewish and other millets on the eve of World War I — Anatolia, the Levant, Mesopotamia and the remaining Balkans before the empire dissolved.
maps.source: Ottoman official statistics and millet estimates, c. 1881–1914 (vilayet yearbooks / 1914 demographic compilations).
maps.statusNote: Needs historic administrative GIS (uyezd / vilayet / kreis / district polygons) matched to period census tables. Borders from today’s maps would be misleading — we are waiting on open historic boundary files (e.g. Heidelberg 1897 / Ristat), which are behind archive download walls from this build environment.

maps.title: Nationalities in Austria-Hungary, c. 1910
maps.blurb: Interactive Dual Monarchy map: toggle Empire / Austria / Hungary, switch ethnicity · population · density layers, and dig into district group mixes (e.g. Bratislavský). Minority enclaves included — Sudeten, Szekler, Saxon, southern Slovak Hungarian belt.
